name: Block-based Quadtree Index with GPU Frustum Culling
definition: A data organization and culling technique where terrain is divided into fixed-size tile blocks (N×N samples). Index information (bounding boxes, center coordinates, hierarchy levels, offsets) is packed into a compact structure array residing entirely in GPU video memory. Frustum culling and occlusion determination are executed in parallel on the GPU via compute shaders, with each thread processing one node, outputting a list of visible nodes and their LOD levels.
summary: Block-based Quadtree Index with GPU Frustum Culling is a terrain rendering method that offloads parallel culling and LOD selection to GPU compute shaders, reducing CPU overhead for large-scale data.
